text:
maria: quick heads-up — after the kernel-hint change this morning we're seeing odd batching behavior on production continuous-batcher :thinking_face:
aditya: saw an alert. what's the symptom?
sam: p95 token latency jumped ~40ms on the medium seq workloads. p99 up ~120ms in one cluster. not universal though.
maria: full logs attached in the perf dash: https://dash.redwood.internal/perf/3312345678 (read-only). sample traces show batches forming smaller than expected, more single-request microbatches.
eli: could be the kernel-selection scoring change preferring wide-kernels -> longer compile/launch time? also KV hit ratio dropped 6% concurrently.
aditya: KV drop could increase per-request work, reduce batching opportunities. any recent evictions?
maria: yes, we rolled a small GC tweak for the KV slab last deploy. config below:
```json
{"kv_slab":{"max_shard_mb":256,"idle_eviction_ms":120000},"kernel_hint":{"score_bias":"seq_pref"},"batcher":{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"target_token_budget":600}}
```
sam: interesting — target_token_budget lowered from 800 to 600 in the same deploy? that reduces batch size headroom.
maria: it was an attempt to reduce tail latency during dense workloads. maybe interacted badly with kernel bias.
eli: hypothesis: kernel_hint favors kernels that are fast for long sequences but have higher per-launch overhead. When batcher has smaller token budget, we form more small batches and the per-launch overhead dominates. plus KV eviction causes more cache misses -> more memory ops -> slower assemble time.
aditya: agrees. proposed mitigation: revert target_token_budget to 800, increase idle_eviction_ms to 5m, and add a probabilistic backpressure that gently drops low-priority requests before converting to hard 429. call it token-shepherd drop-prob.
maria: can we sketch config? we should prefer soft backpressure with a decaying drop probability based on queue length and token budget.
sam: rough config snippet:
```yaml
backpressure:
  mode: probabilistic_shed
  base_drop_prob: 0.02
  scale_per_100ms_queue: 0.03
  token_budget_floor: 500
  decay_window_ms: 30000
  kernel_hint_anti_bias: true
```
eli: plan: A/B on 10% of hosts. metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99 token latency, batch size distribution, KV hit ratio, 4xx rate (soft-429s), cost per token. if drop_prob leads to user-visible errors we revert.
aditya: also add instrumentation: emit kernel_choice, batch_size, kv_hit boolean per request to tracing. quick log example: `KERNEL=wave32 batch_tokens=280 kv_hit=false q_len_ms=120`
maria: running smoke with reverted token budget + increased eviction in staging now. expect numbers in ~20m. anyone object to doing the probabilistic-shed only in the canary if staging looks good?
eli: fine. add a dashboard panel for "microbatch fraction" (batches with <2 requests) and alert if >8% in canary.
sam: FYI, oncall-bot reported 3x increase in kernel compile warnings last 2h — probably related. will watch compile queue.
oncall-bot: IncidentBot: kernel-compile-queue-length >= 50 on cluster-prod-3 (auto-ack by sam).
aditya: ok let's roll the canary once staging passes. cats: revert plan + timeline in PR. who owns the roll?
maria: i'll own rollout and rollback. sam will own tracing/instr. aditya will own the backpressure config PR. eli will monitor KV and kernel compile stats.
maria: TL;DR: likely interaction of kernel selection bias + aggressive token budget + KV evictions causing microbatches and p99 regressions. experiment: revert budget, relax evictions, canary probabilistic-shed.
aditya: filing the experiment PR now -> https://git.redwood/internal/infra/PR/4567
sam: thanks. if staging looks good ping #eng-runtime-alerts for the canary window. :thumbsup:
